                                APPLICATION OF QUEEN BEE SOLAR 1 LLC
                       FOR A CERTIFICATE OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY

                      Queen Bee Solar 1 LLC (the "Applicant"), by its undersigned counsel, hereby submits this

             Application to the Maryland Public Service Commission (the "Commission") for a Certificate of

             Public Convenience and Necessity ("CPCN") (the "Application") to construct a 5.00 megawatt

             alternating current ("MWac"), single-axis tracker community solar energy generating facility and

             associated interconnection facilities located in Prince George's County, Maryland (the "Queen

             Bee Solar Project" or "Project") pursuant to Md. Public Utilities Article ("PUA")§§ 7-207 and 7-

             218.

                      The Application is comprised of this petition together with the attached Environmental

             Review Document ("ERD") and associated appendices. Section I of this petition provides an

             overview of the Project; Section II summarizes how the Project meets the statutory criteria for

             granting a CPCN as required by PUA §§ 7-207 and 7-218; and Section III summarizes the

             Application information required by COMAR 20.79.01.06. 1




             1 PUA § 7-208(c) requires an applicant to provide notice two years prior to construction of a generating station and

             any associated overhead transmission lines designed to carry a voltage in excess of 69 kV unless the Commission
             waives the two-year notice requirement. Here, the Project will interconnect at less than 69 kV. Accordingly, the Project
             does not invoke the notice requirement of PUA § 7-208(c).
                                 I. PROJECT INTRODUCTION

       The Project is proposed at 17308 Queen Anne Bridge Road, Bowie, Maryland 20716. The

Project has an approximately 34-acre limit of construction and an approximately 23-acre fenced

area within an approximately 55-acre portion (the "Solar Property") of an approximately 84.88-

acre parcel identified as Tax Map 0064, Grid 00A3, Parcel 0002 in Prince George's County,

Maryland (the "Parent Property"). ERD at § 2 and Tables 2-3. The Parent Property is located

within the County' s Agriculture and Preservation ("AG") zone and is currently in agricultural use.

Approximately 1.3 acres within the limit of construction are classified as prime farmland, and no

farmland of statewide importance is located within the limit of construction. ERD at Tables 3 and

12. The owner of the Parent Property (the "Landowner") independently plans to subdivide the

Parent Property and the Project has been sited to avoid interfering with that planned subdivision.

ERD at§ 2.

       The Project will be a 5.00 MWac photovoltaic generating station that will allocate energy

to community solar subscribers within Baltimore Gas and Electric Company ("BGE") service

territory. The Project will interconnect at 33 kV with BGE feeder 33753 along Mill Branch Road.

ERD at §§ 2.F and 2.L.

       During the construction phase, which is estimated to last six months, the Project is expected

to involve approximately $13 million in capital investment and to support approximately 33 direct

construction jobs and 58 indirect jobs. The Project is also expected to support one direct job and

one indirect job during operation. ERD at§§ 2.K and 5.L and Appendix K.

       Maryland requires 50% of electricity sales to be supported by renewable energy credits by

2030, including 14.5% from solar energy by 2028. The Project will contribute 5.00 MWac of

community solar generation toward those requirements.




                                                 2
 ,

            In summary, there are compelling economic, environmental, and legal reasons for the State

    and the Commission to expeditiously approve this CPCN application, with no countervailing harm .

    Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests that the Commission expeditiously approve the

    Project.

                                            11. CPCN STAND ARD

               When the Commission considers whether to grant a CPCN, it must take into account "the

    effect of the generating station .. . on:

               (i)    the stability and reliability of the electric system;
               (ii)   economics;
               (iii)  esthetics;
               (iv)   historic sites;
               (v)    aviation safety as determined by the Maryland Aviation Administration and the
               administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration;
               (vi)   when applicable, air and water pollution; and
               (vii) the availability of means for the required timely disposal of wastes produced by any
               generating station."

    PUA § 7-207(e)(2). In addition, the Commission must consider "the effect of climate change on

    the generating station ... based on the best available scientific information recognized by the

    Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change." PUA § 7-207(e)(3).                 The Commission must

    consider:

               (4) for a generating station:
                       (i)      the consistency of the application with the comprehensive plan and zoning
                       of each county or municipal corporation where any portion of the generating station
                       is proposed to be located;
                       (ii)     the efforts to resolve any issues presented by a county or municipal
                       corporation where any portion of the generating station is proposed to be located;
                       (iii)    the impact of the generating station on the quantity of annual and long-term
                       statewide greenhouse gas emissions, measured in the manner specified in § 2-1202
                       of the Environment Article and based on the best available scientific information
                        recognized by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change; and
                       (iv)     the consistency of the application with the State's climate commitments for
                        reducing statewide greenhouse gas emissions, including those specified in Title 2,
                        Subtitle 12 of the Environment Article.




                                                         3
                   PUA§ 7-207(e)(4).

         Finally, as of July 1, 2025, the Commission must consider, "for a solar energy generating

station specified under § 7-218 of this subtitle, whether the owner of a proposed solar energy

generating station complies with the site requirements under§ 7-218(f) of this subtitle." PUA§ 7-

207(e)(5). 2

         The attached ERD provides significant detail as to all applicable factors, but in summary,

each such factor weighs heavily in favor of granting the Applicant's requested CPCN.

         With respect to zoning, the Parent Property is located within the AG zone of Prince

George's County. ERD at§ 2.B. A large-scale solar energy system is permitted by right in the AG

zone under Prince George's County Code§ 27-5 lOl(c), subject to the use-specific standards of§

27-5102(d)(6)(A) addressing lot coverage, access, height, solar easements, scenic and historic

viewsheds, and shielded inverter equipment. The Project satisfies each of these standards,

including a lot coverage of approximately 41 percent of the Solar Property (below the 65 percent

maximum), a maximum height of approximately 15 feet (below the County's 20-foot maximum),

and compliance with the County Landscape Manual ' s buffering requirements for Mill Branch

Road, a designated scenic and historic roadway. The Project has also been designed to comply

with the County' s solar energy system fire safety requirements, including a ten-foot non-

combustible perimeter surface. ERD at § 2.B. The Project is consistent with Plan 2035, the

County' s General Plan, including its policies to improve water quality through stormwater

management, minimize light spillover, meet State noise standards, and encourage investment in

renewable and low-carbon energy generation. ERD at § 2.B.



2 PUA§ 7-218 applies to the Project because it is more than 1 MWac, is a community solar energy generating

system, and is not located on a rooftop, carport, or brownfields site or behind the meter of a retail electric customer.
PUA § 7-218(b).


                                                            4
        Under PUA§ 7-218(h)(l)(i), a local jurisdiction may not adopt zoning laws or other laws

or regulations that prohibit construction or operation of solar energy generating stations. Under

PUA § 7-218(h)(2)(ii), a local jurisdiction must process the site development plan for a solar

project not larger than 5 MWac as a permitted use. Because large-scale solar energy systems are

permitted by right in the AG zone and the Project has been designed to meet the County's use-

specific standards, the Applicant is not requesting preemption of any County zoning requirement.

The Project will maintain a minimum 150-foot setback from the nearest wall of a residential

dwelling, a minimum 100-foot setback from all property lines, and a setback of more than 450 feet

from Mill Branch Road. The Applicant is proposing a game fence at least six feet in height that

will not use barbed wire and will not be located within 50 feet of a public road right-of-way. ERD

at§§ 2.B and 2.D.

       The Project is located within the County' s Priority Preservation Area ("PPA"). Consistent

with the County ' s 2017 Resource Conservation Plan, the fenced Project area has been located

outside of areas containing prime farmland soils, and prime farmland within the limit of

construction has been minimized. Pursuant to PUA § 7-2 l 8(h)(4), solar development within a PPA

is limited to 5% of the PPA ' s total acreage, and the Applicant has received confirmation that

existing and proposed solar development within the PPA remains below that threshold. ERD at §

2.B and Appendix B.

       The Applicant provided Prince George' s County with an initial draft of the ERD, including

a conceptual plan, on June I 0, 2026 and requested both a meeting with County staff and a

preliminary report regarding the Project's consistency with the County's comprehensive plan and

zoning ordinance. The County confirmed receipt of the documents and included its Public

Facilities Team for awareness. ERD at § l .F and Appendix B. In addition, the Project is subject to




                                                 5
                                                                                                        ...




review by the Prince George' s County Planning Board through the Mandatory Referral process

under Md. Land Use Article §§ 20-301 et seq ., which will proceed alongside the CPCN process.

The Applicant anticipates receiving the Planning Board' s Mandatory Referral recommendations

by early 2027, in advance of the direct testimony deadlines for the Power Plant Research Program

("PPRP"), Commission Staff, and the Office of People' s Counsel. ERD at§ 2.B.

       Under COMAR 20.62.03.08, the total installed capacity of community solar energy

generating systems located on the same or adjacent parcels is limited to 5 MW. Under the current

parcel configuration, the Parent Property is adjacent to a parcel hosting Bulldog Solar One, LLC,

a 2 MWac community solar facility placed in service in 2022 under the Community Solar Pilot

Program. Accordingly, the Commission granted the Project's community solar authorization

subject to the Project incorporating agrivoltaics in accordance with COMAR 20.62.03 .08(8)(9)(c).

Upon completion of the Landowner' s planned subdivision, which predates and is independent of

the Project and is anticipated to be completed by early 2027, the parcel containing the Project will

no longer be adjacent to the Bulldog Solar One, LLC parcel. Following completion of the

subdivision, the Applicant anticipates providing the updated parcel configuration to the

Commission and will file documentation of the completed subdivision in this proceeding. As a

contingency, in the event the subdivision is not completed as anticipated, the Applicant has

provided an Agrivoltaics Plan demonstrating how the Project would satisfy the applicable

agrivoltaics requirements. The Applicant will file a Maryland Department of Agriculture-approved

Agrivoltaics Plan in this docket at least 30 days prior to construction. ERD at § 2.C and Appendices

Hand AD.

       The Project is subject to, and has been designed to comply with, the State's siting and

design standards under PUA § 7-218(f). As detailed in the ERD, the Project will provide the




                                                 6
 required residential and property line setbacks; use non-barbed wire fencing; provide a landscaping

buffer where existing wooded vegetation does not provide the required screening; mitigate visual

impacts on the surrounding Priority Preservation Area, Mill Branch Road, and nearby historic

resources; not exceed an average height of 15 feet; minimize grading and retain all topsoil on-site;

plant native ground cover and limit mowing and herbicide use; emit no visible light from dusk to

dawn; and post a landscaping bond with the County for the first five years. The Applicant has also

provided a viewshed analysis as required for solar energy generating stations larger than 2 MWac.

ERD at § 2.D and Appendices A, F, and I.

       Regulatory agencies, including the Maryland Department of the Environment ("MDE"),

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers ("USACE"), Department of Natural Resources ("DNR"), U.S. Fish

and Wildlife Service ("USFWS"), Maryland Historical Trust ("MHT"), and Maryland Aviation

Administration ("MAA''), have reviewed or commented on the Project. Those reviews address

wetlands and waterways, threatened and endangered species, forest conservation, aviation, cultural

resources, and other environmental matters. ERD at§§ 1.E, 3.D, 4.A-C, 5.A, and 5.H.

       The Project will employ Environmental Site Design through non-rooftop disconnection

consistent with MDE' s stormwater design guidance for solar panels, with level spreaders where

panels are placed on slopes between 5% and 10% and grading to reduce slopes exceeding 10%.

Because soils on the site include Marlboro Clay, infiltration practices will be avoided, and the

Project will be designed for the 100-year storm consistent with the County ' s Stormwater

Management Design Manual. The Project will minimize grading, retain all topsoil on-site,

establish a native pervious ground cover beneath the panels, and add approximately 1.65 acres of

impervious surface. The Applicant will obtain coverage under MDE' s NPDES General Permit for

Construction Activity prior to construction. ERD at§§ 2.D, 3.A, and 3.F and Table 10.




                                                 7
        The Project's anticipated useful life is approximately 25 to 40 years. At the end of the

Project' s useful life, equipment will be removed and the land restored to a condition substantially

similar to its pre-construction condition pursuant to a Decommissioning Plan secured by a surety

bond or similar surety. ERD at§§ 2.1 and 3.I.

       Existing vegetation provides effective visual screening along the Project's northern,

western, and the majority of its eastern borders and will remain. Where existing vegetation does

not provide adequate screening, along portions of the southern and eastern borders, a 30-foot wide

Prince George 's County Type C landscape buffer consisting of native deciduous and evergreen

trees and shrubs will be planted to provide four-season screening. Plantings will be maintained

with a 90% survival threshold, and a landscaping bond will be posted with the County. The

viewshed analysis demonstrates that the Project will have very limited visual impact on adjoining

properties. ERD at§§ 2.D and 5.J and Appendices A, F, and I.

       The Project has been designed to avoid impacts to wetlands and waterways. Field

investigations identified five palustrine emergent wetlands totaling approximately 0.06 acres and

four intermittent or ephemeral streams on the Parent Property, all of which, along with their

associated buffers, are located outside the limit of construction. MDE and USACE conducted a

site visit on September 14, 2026 and indicated that the Project will receive a No Permit Required

letter, which the Applicant will file in this docket once received. The Project is not located within

a FEMA floodplain . ERD at§§ 3.A, 3.D, and 3.G and Appendices P- R.

       The Project is located within the Patuxent River watershed (Maryland 8-digit watershed

02131104), approximately 4,400 feet from the Patuxent River, a designated Scenic River. The

Project is outside the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area and is not located within a Tier II watershed.

No waterway or floodplain disturbances are proposed. The groundwater table was confirmed to be




                                                  8
 below the depth of anticipated excavations, and no construction dewatering is anticipated; if

dewatering is required, it would fall within the applicable exemption criteria. ERD at§§ 3.A, 3.F,

3.H, and 4.E and Appendix V.

       The closest inventoried historic property to the Project is Maple Wood, which is located

on the Parent Property. MHT determined that the Project will have no adverse effect on significant

archaeological resources and that further archaeological investigations are not recommended. With

respect to the historic built environment, MHT has requested a Determination of Eligibility

("DOE") to evaluate whether Maple Wood Farm is eligible for listing in the National Register of

Historic Places, and the Applicant expects to submit the completed DOE to MHT by the end of

October. The Landowner has independently determined to demolish the Maple Wood house and

associated outbuildings due to their deteriorated and structurally unsound condition, regardless of

whether the Project is developed. The Applicant will review any recommendations by MHT and

will continue to coordinate with MHT. The next closest historic property, the Queen Anne

Schoolhouse, is approximately 2,900 feet from the Project area and is screened by an established

forest stand. ERD at§ 5.A and Appendix X.

       With respect to electric system stability and reliability, the Applicant was granted Project

capacity under Subscriber Organization Identification Number 26A327920009644 on September

4, 2026. The Applicant submitted a Level 4 interconnection request to BGE (queue number BGE-

9996998) and has received Conditional Approval to interconnect 5 MWac on BGE feeder 33753.

The Project will not be required to undergo the PJM generator interconnection process. ERD at§§

2.K and 2.L and Appendices H and L.

       The Point oflnterconnection is a splice box along Mill Branch Road. BGE will extend, and

reconductor as necessary, its existing three-phase 33 kV feeder along Mill Branch Road to the




                                                9
 Point of Interconnection, and the Project will connect to the Point of Interconnection through

horizontally directionally drilled conduit. BGE's required upstream upgrades include installing a

DA recloser, bi-directional substation metering, and protection equipment, and updating existing

equipment settings. ERD at §§ 2.F and 2.L and Appendices L-M.

       The glare analysis evaluated Mill Branch Road, Queen Anne Bridge Road, the private road

to the south of the Parent Property, and adjacent residential buildings and predicted no glare. There

are no airports within three miles of the Project, the Project does not meet the FAA's notice criteria,

and MAA determined that the Project is not an obstruction or hazard to air navigation. ERD at§§

5.G and 5.H and Appendices AA-AB.

        Waste generated during construction will be collected and removed to an approved waste

handling facility. Operational waste will be minimal and removed during maintenance activities.

Decommissioning waste will be handled under a decommissioning plan that the Applicant will

submit for PPRP review during the CPCN process and that will be approved by the Commission

as a licensing condition. The Applicant further acknowledges that it will be subject to the statewide

decommissioning requirements established under PUA § 7-218 and finalized in Case No. 9873.

ERD at§§ 2.1 and 3.I.

        The Project will emit no air pollutants during operation. Using EPA's A VERT tool, the

ERD estimates that the 5.00 MWac Project will reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately

340 tons per year in Maryland and approximately 6,370 tons per year in the Mid-Atlantic region.

Over its estimated 30-year operating life, the Project is estimated to reduce carbon dioxide

emissions by approximately 9,726 tons in Maryland and 182,231 tons in the Mid-Atlantic region .

ERD at§ 3.E.

        The Project will provide economic benefits through an estimated $13 million capital




                                                  10
 I




    investment, approximately 33 direct construction jobs and 58 indirect jobs during construction,

    and one direct and one indirect job during operation. The Project will also generate County tax

    revenue in the form of personal property taxes assessed on the value of the solar facility and will

    provide subscribers with access to clean energy and reduced electricity bills. ERD at §§ 2.K and

                                                                                                           Mandatory Referral Process
                                                                                                           Because the Project requires a CPCN under Public Utilities Article § 7-207, the Maryland
                                                                                                           Public Service Commission has jurisdiction over the siting and construction of the Project,
                                                                                                           rather than the Project being subject to the County's ordinary local zoning approval process.
                                                                                                           Separately, pursuant to Land Use Article§§ 20-301 et seq., the Project is subject to review by
                                                                                                           the Prince George's County Planning Board through the Mandatory Referral process.

                                                                                                           Mandatory referral does not constitute a separate or independent local land-use approval
                                                                                                           that the Project must obtain apart from the CPCN. Rather, it is the mechanism by which the
                                                                                                           Planning Board transmits its recommendations, testimony, and any master plan or zoning
                                                                                                           consistency findings into the Commission's record for consideration alongside the other
                                                                                                  )        factors under PUA § 7-207[e). The County's mandatory referral review, like the
                                                                                                           recommendation of the local governing body itself, informs the Commission's ultimate siting
                                                                                                           decision rather than constraining or duplicating it. As such, this process will occur alongside
                                                                                                           the state's CPCN process with at least one full submission and review cycle to be completed
                                                                                                           prior to the Project's evidentiary hearing as part of the CPCN process.

                                                                                                           In order to proceed through the Mandatory Referral process, the Applicant will submit the
                                                                                                           required plans and environmental materials to Prince George's County, including the Natural
                                                                                                           Resource Inventory/Forest Stand Delineation and Stormwater Management Concept Plan.
                                                                                                           The Applicant anticipates being able to submit the Mandatory Referral Site Plan in the next
                                                                                                           4-6 months following the completion of the Landowner's minor subdivision. Following
                                                                                                           submission, the Project will undergo a 60-day coordinated interagency review and public
                                                                                                           comment period, culminating in a Planning Board public hearing and issuance of an advisory
                                                                                                           recommendation. The Applicant anticipates receiving Mandatory Referral recommendations
                                                                                                           by early 2027 in advance of PPRP/Staff/OPC direct testimony deadlines (pending the
                                                                                                           Project's Procedural Schedule to be set) Following Mandatory Referral and issuance of a
                                                                                                           CPCN, the Applicant will coordinate with DPIE and other applicable County agencies to obtain
                                                                                                           the necessary permits and approvals for construction.
